title: Keep lit-hemisphere close-world motion and comparable scale on all screen shapes

scope.subject: Repair Approach–Orbit responsive framing and wheel-driven camera yaw at the signed azimuth seam; verify the actual applied midpoint without changing the release gates.

research_summary: The checked-in registry and existing viewport-framing research identify YEIS, R3F, ProceduralPlanets and camera-controls as the current authorities. Inspected installed Drei camera-controls 2.10.x and root v3: lerpLookAt subtracts the independently wrapped endpoint angles. Negative-Z Approach and Orbit straddle -pi/+pi, causing a long sweep across the dark side. Independent PR-head trace shows measured normalized radii near 0.204 and 0.362: the uncapped ultrawide bonus amplifies the variance. Reuse the existing fit-sphere floor, existing cinematic anchors and Three vector interpolation; no new controls, broader light changes, renderer, or adjustment to acceptance thresholds.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS remains the universe/navigation mother product; the defect is local world framing after arrival, not a reason to replace the cross-scale engine.
React Three Fiber remains the shared Canvas lifecycle and camera host; world framing should stay inside the existing scene rather than add another render surface.

The exact installed camera-controls line exposes getDistanceToFitSphere(radius), which derives a perspective-camera fit distance from effective FOV and aspect ratio, and setLookAt for preserving the desired viewing direction. The installed Drei 9 control is backed by camera-controls 2.x; its lerpLookAt subtracts wrapped spherical azimuths without first unwrapping. Its setLookAt and sphere-fit APIs remain suitable.

The adopted planet subsystem renders ordinary worlds at the project-defined scene radius; framing should adapt the existing camera to that radius instead of changing the planet renderer or destination model.
Reuse existing Three vector direction and distance interpolation on nearby authored world directions; no new camera subsystem.

search_ladder.conclusion: Keep YEIS as the full universe and cross-scale navigation solution; only the product-world camera framing layer needs correction.
Keep the single R3F Canvas and its current camera lifecycle.
Keep the existing world renderer and shared scene radius; changing visual generation would not solve fixed-camera aspect-ratio overflow.
Reuse the already-shipped camera-controls fit-distance calculation instead of maintaining custom FOV/aspect trigonometry or a second camera controller.

candidates.name: Pinned MIT YEIS world/navigation backbone
candidates.license: MIT source at pinned e520568 with retained asset notices
candidates.reason: Retains the authoritative destination and cross-scale semantics, but the React product-world camera is intentionally project-owned.

candidates.name: Existing React Three Fiber camera host
candidates.reason: Provides the single camera/render lifecycle and viewport updates; it does not itself select a world framing distance.

candidates.name: camera-controls v3 viewport-aware sphere fit distance
candidates.source: Existing Drei CameraControls dependency backed by camera-controls v3.1.2
candidates.reason: Directly solves the observed aspect-ratio framing failure using the already-shipped camera authority: derive final shot radius from getDistanceToFitSphere while retaining current shot direction and transition semantics.

candidates.name: Project-owned manual FOV/aspect fit formula
candidates.reason: Would duplicate the exact tested fit-distance primitive already present in camera-controls and create another source of camera geometry truth.

decision.rationale: Keep the current renderer, light axis, navigation and single controls owner. Compose a shortest-direction path just for the affected fitted world shots, keep the existing fit-sphere safety constraint and compose primarily by viewport height; remove the ultrawide bonus rather than enlarging the world to hide the wrong-side interpolation.
decision.fallback: If overlay-safe composition still needs adjustment after viewport-aware fitting, use camera-controls focal offset or fit padding as a second narrow refinement rather than restoring hard-coded per-device shot coordinates.
